subject: Fwd: Package data unavailable until after calling library(package_name)

messages.author: 38f9cffaa23acd56
messages.subject: Fwd: Package data unavailable until after calling library(package_name)
parts:
Hi all,

I'm having trouble with making some package data available both to functions within a package and to users of the package, without forcing them to call "library(my_package)" first. I have a detailed description, followed by my question and a link to a reproducible example below.

We've been developing a package (let's call it myPackageTest) that needs access to some a precalculated data frame (call it public_data).

This data is stored as a .rda file in the data folder of the package. It is documented in the data.R file in the data folder of the package.

If I open a clean R workspace and run the command myPackageTest::public_data, without running library(myPackageTest) first, it works and I can see the data frame. Great!

However, I have function my_function which relies on public_data. If I then call myPackageTest::my_function(), I get:

Error in myPackageTest::my_function() : 
  object 'public_data' not found

If I call library(myPackageTest), then repeat my call to my_function(), everything works and the data is found.

If I switch the format of the data to .Rdata from .rda, as Hadley Wickham's package guide says we should, then it's available nowhere, not even after calling "library(myPackageTest".

I've been able to make it so that package functions can access the data whether the user has called "library" or not by switching the data to internal data stored in sysdata.rda, but then the data isn't available directly to package users if I want them to have it too. I haven't seen anything indicating that data the package exports isn't available within the package (but I'm beginning to suspect this)

So, my question - is there a solution that makes package data:
  1. work within package functions without the need to use "library(myPackageTest)" (I want other R libraries to be able to use it that can't/shouldn't call "library")
  2. makes the data available to users of the package
Maybe I'm looking at this wrong? The real code and a minimal reproducible example that matches what I've shared here are both stored at https://github.com/ceff-tech/ffc_api_client/tree/packageTest

Thanks for any help you can provide - I hope my question and problem description are clear - I'd be happy to clarify anything.

Nick Santos
